categories.main_business_segments: Maxio Technology (Hangzhou) Co., Ltd. primarily operates in two main business segments: data storage controller chips and AIoT signal processing and transmission chips. The company designs and sells integrated circuit chips, focusing on SSD controller chips for consumer, industrial, and enterprise applications, as well as AIoT chips used in smart home, automotive electronics, industrial IoT, and public IoT sectors.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company employs advanced SoC chip architecture design, algorithm design, digital and analog IP design, and mid-to-back-end design technologies. It has proprietary technologies including advanced error correction codes (LDPC), protocol controllers (SATA, PCIe, NVMe, UFS), data security IP, high-speed interface IPs, and automated testing systems. Production is outsourced via a fabless model, with wafer fabrication, packaging, and testing handled by third-party foundries and subcontractors.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include SSD module manufacturers, PC OEMs, server and system manufacturers, and AIoT device makers in sectors such as consumer electronics, industrial control, data communication, smart homes, automotive electronics, and public infrastructure. The company serves both domestic and international markets, with products sold in over 60 countries and regions.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in China, with significant sales both within mainland China and internationally. Overseas sales accounted for approximately 44% of revenue. It has subsidiaries in Guangzhou, Suzhou, Chengdu, and Hong Kong, supporting its R&D and sales operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Maxio Technology operates as a fabless semiconductor design company, focusing on chip design and sales. It outsources wafer fabrication, packaging, and testing to third-party foundries and subcontractors, positioning itself upstream in the semiconductor supply chain as a design and IP provider.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company prioritizes continuous innovation in data storage controller chips and AIoT signal processing and transmission chips. It invests heavily in R&D (over 36% of revenue), focusing on next-generation PCIe 5.0 SSD controllers, embedded storage controllers (UFS/eMMC), and AIoT chips including automotive-grade and Ethernet PHY chips. It aims to expand product portfolios, improve performance, reduce power consumption, and deepen market penetration in emerging AIoT applications.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of self-designed integrated circuit chips, including SSD controller chips and AIoT chips. The company also provides related technical services such as chip design and firmware customization. Sales are conducted mainly via direct sales to end customers and supplemented by distributors.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Maxio Technology is a leading independent SSD controller chip provider globally, ranking among the top in shipment volume. It competes with NAND flash manufacturers with in-house controllers (Samsung, Micron, Western Digital), other independent controller vendors like Silicon Motion, Realtek, and emerging players. In AIoT chips, it is in the early stage but competes against established international giants like Marvell and Realtek.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, the company achieved revenue of approximately RMB 1.17 billion, a 13.55% increase year-over-year, with net profit attributable to shareholders reaching RMB 118 million, up 126%. Total assets grew to over RMB 2.08 billion, reflecting rapid expansion fueled by a successful IPO raising over RMB 1 billion. The company maintains a strong growth trajectory with increasing R&D investment and expanding market share.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Maxio Technology emphasizes its proprietary core technologies, high integration, and performance in SSD controller chips, offering high reliability, low power consumption, and broad NAND compatibility. Its AIoT chips integrate advanced signal processing and transmission capabilities, including automotive-grade safety features and Ethernet PHY integration. The company leverages a comprehensive SoC design platform to deliver cost-effective, scalable, and innovative chip solutions that meet evolving market demands across consumer, industrial, and automotive sectors.
